variant_reviews.comparison: Z is the LOCATION attaining the maximum of W(t)-t^2 over all real t, not the maximum value or the argmax of a differently scaled drift. IsBrownianReal is indexed by nonnegative real time; a two-sided standard process needs compatible independent positive and negative Brownian halves joined at zero, not the same path reflected on both sides. IsMaxOn describes a maximizing point but gives no global attainment on the noncompact real line, a.s. uniqueness or measurable selection. Those require Brownian growth and argmax results beyond the inspected primitives. Measure.map gives the law only for an a.e.-measurable location map; its fallback must not hide a failed selection. The source's approximately 0.26 variance is a quoted property of this normalization and is not certified numerically by these declarations. Library Chernoff exponential tail bounds concern a different object.
